symptom: `snippetcall sc (snippet: M.S, class: 'x')` / `alter page M.P { set (Class: 'x') on sc }` passed check, exec and mx check (0 errors) and describe showed the class, but nothing in the running app carried it (mendixlabs/mxcli#1511)
cause: Not an mxcli defect: a Forms$SnippetCallWidget renders no DOM element - the snippet's widgets are inlined into the parent - so its Appearance (Class, Style, DynamicClasses, DesignProperties) has nothing to land on. Measured on 11.15.0 with run --local (hsqldb) + playwright check: .probe-x / .probe-dyn / the red border / pull-right / hide-tablet = 0 elements; the snippet's own container was a direct child of the enclosing container; a container on the same page with the same four settings carried all of them (control)
file: `mdl/executor/validate_snippetcall_appearance.go` (MDL-WIDGET48: `validateSnippetCallAppearance` in the widget-tree walk for CREATE / ALTER INSERT / REPLACE; `validateStoredSnippetCallAppearance` in the reference pass for ALTER PAGE SET and ALTER STYLING, typed via `widgetStorageTyper`), `mdl/linter/rules/snippet_call_appearance.go` (MPR013: catalog Class/Style/DynamicClasses + design properties read from the raw unit)
insight: **Valid BSON, a clean mx check and a correct describe prove nothing about whether an appearance setting renders** - only the DOM does. The positive control (same settings on a container on the same page) is what makes a 0-count meaningful: without it a stale build or a wrong selector reads the same. ALTER ... SET names a STORED widget, so whether it is a snippet call is only answerable against the document; `widgetStorageTyper` (pagemutator) already gives the $Type, so the check runs in the reference pass and appends a warning (never blocks). Clearing a class on a snippet call is the fix and must stay silent.
